answer: A logistics network curbs Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to physical transceivers anchored at a marine wharf. To authenticate, an agent decodes phase-shifted flashes from a harbor lantern synchronized with orbital telemetry from a deep-space comet monitor. An adversary incurs the scarce hardware and maintenance cost of dedicated physical sensors per persona rather than virtualizing instances. However, coastal fog can attenuate the optical signal, erroneously locking out valid agents.
